findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.comment: Facility was observed to have no written policy or bleach available for responding to vomit/diarrheal events. The PIC was informed and plans to purchase bleach. A procedural handout was provided. Bleach was acquired during today’s visit.
findings.citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed soda syrup boxes to be stored directly on the ground in the kitchen. The PIC was informed that food items must be stored at least 6” off the ground to prevent cross-contamination. Milk crates and plastic pallets are adequate for storage. Ensure these items are stored correctly prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.
